evidence: In all three 3D views every body (RJ45 jack, QFP, crystal, headers, passives) renders as a distinct separated volume with visible board surface between neighbors, including the tight C1/R3/C2 cluster left of U1.
In 3d_iso and 3d_iso_back all bodies sit flush on the PCB surface with no floating, sinking, or tilt, including the tall RJ45 jack and both pin headers.
In 3d_top the QFP leads land centered on their pad rows, the crystal and surrounding passives sit on their footprints, and the RJ45 body is centered between its visible shield pads.

The RJ45 jack opens outward over the board edge (orange contacts face off-board in 3d_iso_back), the vertical pin headers J2/J3 mate from above, and there are no relays or visibly polarized parts to misorient.

The bottom ~40% of the board is empty while passives crowd U1 with overlapping designators (C1/R3 stacked, R1R2C3 jammed), and headers J2/J3 float mid-board far from any edge or group, so the layout reads as one congested cluster plus strays rather than tidy grid-aligned groups.
